Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-08-24 | AMZN | Underweight | -0.9% | -1.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: reduce roughly one-third of a standard position, do not exit, and do not add. Sell the first half of the trim at market near 262.07 (split it — 262.01 is contested by six cents against a $7.28 ATR), and place the balance into a rally at 266.40–267.41 (VWMA) or on a daily close below 257.04, whichever comes first. Carry the residual at 60–70% of standard weight — roughly 55–65 shares-equivalent of the ~91-share 1.5-ATR cap per $100k book — and halve it again to ~30–35% through the 08/26 NVDA print and Jackson Hole, or overlay a sized 30–45 day 250/240 put spread instead of selling blind. Hard de-risk below 257.04 on >45M shares; take the residual to minimum on a break of the rising 50-SMA at 250.14. Horizon 1–3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The bear won on the one item that carried the whole bull case, and won it with arithmetic rather than assertion: the valuation pillar. The bull's §5 rested entirely on "21.3x forward, one turn above the S&P." $262.07 ÷ 21.3 = ~$12.30, which is essentially the reported TTM EPS ($135.3B / ~10.89B shares ≈ $12.4) — the same number inflated by the $62.8B H1 equity mark-up the bull had just told the room to discard. Recompute on the bull's own adjusted base ($1.96 in Q2, $3.68 in H1 → ~$7.3–7.8 annualized) and AMZN is 33–36x clean earnings, roughly fifteen turns above the index, with negative free cash flow and zero buyback across every period examined — no company bid under the stock. You cannot use one EPS base for the growth claim and a different one for the divisor. That does not make AMZN a bad business; it makes the advertised "asymmetry" false, and the asymmetry was load-bearing. All three seats converged on that point — the aggressive led with it, the conservative explicitly conceded it, and the neutral accepted it while arguing only about degree.

Three further bear points survived unrefuted and govern sizing rather than direction. First, cash conversion: FCF after acquisitions is −$53.6B, and the bull's "$173B capex" framing skipped $39.8B of H1 M&A and a $106.1B six-month build in non-marketable equity securities to $122.3B — 11.2% of total assets, marked by management's own models, with a $62.8B H1 revaluation the source itself calls "bimodal, not smooth." That is a capital-allocation risk that lands in a single quarter, and no seat produced a disclosure of the mark-to-model assumptions. Second, leverage: the advertised "+$43.1B net cash" is a gross-debt-only construct; adding lease obligations flips it to a net obligation. I state the honest range rather than the headline — the $11.8B finance-lease line may already sit inside the $133B gross debt, so the true figure is likely between −$40B and −$67B, not exactly −$66.7B — but on either arithmetic the cushion is far thinner than a balance sheet that nearly doubled debt in six months deserves. Third, OCF quality: $30.5B of deferred tax plus a $25.5B AP build (payables +20.9% vs revenue +18.2%) plus $10.1B of SBC out of $161.4B means the "2x coverage" of the $78.1B twelve-month contractual ladder is closer to 1.7x, and part of it is vendor financing that unwinds if growth decelerates.

The $650B commitment ladder is what kills the bull's catalyst rather than merely delaying it. The bull needs peak capex to unlock an FCF inflection; the bear is right that the same disclosure cannot simultaneously be a demand signal (spend continues) and a fixed cost (FCF does not inflect). Add D&A +31.3% with $173B of capex not yet fully depreciating, plus an effective tax rate stepping 17% → 23% against a ~4.9% cash tax rate and a $41.4B deferred liability, and the +43.2% operating income growth is not an extrapolable run rate — it is a base effect against an offset that has not yet landed. Also relevant: a +2.5% marketing and −6.0% G&A tape laps within four quarters.

On the tape the edge is modest but it points the same way, and it is stated honestly rather than maximized. The bull's contracting-volume observation is legitimate — 28.07M vs a 32.6M ten-session and 47.0M twenty-one-session average — and I will not pretend otherwise. But the 08-19 push to 266.40 died on 35.8M shares within 1% of the $267.41 VWMA, and 08-17 was rejected on 43.9M: supply was tested and confirmed, not absorbed. Price is six cents above the 262.01 gap roof against a $7.28 ATR — a coin flip, not a held line. Downside references are 250.14 (−4.6%) and the 239.82 gap floor (−8.5%) versus a first real upside reference at 272.27 (+3.9%), into a binary NVDA print on 08/26 with crowded, 13F-lagged long positioning (Druckenmiller, Tepper at 16% of book). That is the wrong shape for a full-weight hold, and neither the neutral's range trade nor the conservative's "protect the residual" framing changes the payoff map.

Why Underweight and not Sell, and why the residual is not token. The operating engine is genuinely strong and no bear falsifier has triggered: revenue +19.6% accelerating from +16.6%, operating income +43.2%, margin 13.7% (+230bps), Q2 OCF +39.6%, AWS's fastest growth in 18 quarters, custom silicon at a $25B run-rate, interest coverage 20.9x, and $176.1B of liquid assets with $96.5B of AFS maturing inside a year at ~par. The technical regime has not broken either: the 50-SMA (250.14) and 200-SMA (238.39) are both rising, the golden cross has held since May 6, RSI never flushed (low 49.74), and the MACD line is still +3.16 above zero. The bear's own falsifiers are plausible, not remote. That is why the conservative's push to cap the residual at 30–35% before the 08/26 event is over-correction: it prices a trend break that has not occurred and would repeat the documented pattern in this name where heavy de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200-SMA structure paid nothing. I side with the neutral on that point, and it is also why the trader's "Sell" label is executed as a partial reduction — Underweight — rather than an exit.

I side with the neutral and the trader on execution and against the aggressive analyst's comfort level: 60–70% residual is defensible, but only with the second half of the tranche placed against supply (266.40–267.41) or against a confirmed break (close below 257.04 on >45M), and only if the event window is explicitly de-risked or hedged with a sized 250/240 put spread matching the bear's two downside references (rising 50-SMA 250.14 and gap floor 239.82). A 257.04 stop is roughly 0.7 ATR from spot with ATR at 7.28 — it bounds intent, not realized loss, so size, not the stop, is the protection.

Prior lessons applied: (1) five-day windows at ~1x ATR are noise and cannot adjudicate a multi-quarter thesis, so the triggers below — not the raw return — are the scorecard; (2) the 2026-08-17 AMZN Underweight returned only +0.3% raw / +1.5% alpha precisely because its tape layer treated one negative session as confirmation, so the tape leg here is sized modestly and the multi-quarter items (valuation, FCF, marks) carry the call; (3) repeated AMZN underweights that de-risked too hard inside a rising structure forfeited alpha, which is why the residual is 60–70% and not 30–35%.

What would change the call. Upgrade to Overweight on any two of: (a) a daily close above $267.41 on volume >45M with a higher low above 262.01; (b) any capex guide-down or evidence of peak spend; (c) TTM FCF or FCF-after-M&A improving from −$11.6B / −$53.6B for two consecutive quarters; (d) gross debt stabilizing near $133B with issuance below ~$5B per quarter; (e) disclosure that a material slice of the $122.3B non-marketable equity book has been realized at those marks. Downgrade to Sell on a close below 257.04 on >45M volume that fails to reclaim 262.01 within 2–3 sessions, on a break of the rising 50-SMA at 250.14, or on any impairment/flat-mark quarter on the $122.3B book. Treat the MACD line crossing zero (now +3.16, histogram −1.47 and expanding) as confirmation of the same signal, not a new decision. Treat 262.01 as a level, not a support — there is no valuation floor and no buyback to lean on.

Data gaps flagged, not papered over: no usable insider data, no social-sentiment data, and 137 of 157 news records are missing for the 8/17–8/21 window — the exact week AMZN fell 8.9% — so any AMZN-specific catalyst from that window is not in evidence. The Rosenblatt $335 target is dated 08/19 and surfaced via an 08/23 round-up and should be treated as stale, not live. No portfolio, holdings, or cash context was supplied, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation; the trim should flex with the caller's aggregate AI-capex concentration elsewhere.

**Price Target**: 250.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print (inventory turns, D&A step-up from $173B capex, whether the 23% effective tax rate holds)

REFLECTION:
Alpha of −1.3% (raw −0.9%) is directionally consistent with an Underweight but sits well inside one ATR of ~2.8%, so the five-day window cannot adjudicate a 1–3 month thesis built on valuation, FCF and the $122.3B mark-to-model book. What it does touch is the tape leg: the 266.40–267.41 supply zone held and price drifted toward the 250.14 reference, supporting the decision to place the second tranche against supply rather than sell blind, while the 60–70% residual and the 257.04 trigger remain untested. Lesson for the next similar call: log the falsifier levels and their volume conditions at inception and grade the review against those triggers, not against a five-day return that is indistinguishable from noise.

[2026-08-21 | AMZN | Underweight | +3.0% | +2.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim 40–50% of any existing position, taking a benchmark 100-unit holding to roughly 50–60 units, and front-load half of that reduction at/near the market (258.63–262.75, with 261.38 Bollinger mid and 262.75 10-EMA as the working limits) rather than pre-committing the whole trim to a bounce the falling 10-EMA may not deliver; the second 10–15% goes only if AMZN fails at 262.75/266.40 or closes below 256.93 on expanding volume. Do not add at 258.63 and do not short — the rising 50-SMA at 249.73 and 200-SMA at 238.33, the intact golden cross and ~30x interest coverage make a relative underweight the higher-quality expression. Note that 269.19 is an invalidation trigger for the tactical sell case, not a "stop loss"; re-engage only on a close above it on >50M shares with a positive MACD histogram plus the next session holding above 266.40, then add back one-quarter to one-third of what was trimmed. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the next 10-Q.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converged on the same action — sell a slice, keep a core, do not short — so the decision is about size and instrumentation, and on both the conservative and neutral seats beat the aggressive one.

Why the direction is settled. The near-term tape is broken and neither of the other two seats contested it: AMZN lost the 07-31 gap low at 262.01, trades 1.57% below the 10-EMA at 262.75 and 4.07% below the VWMA at 269.19 where the gap cohort is trapped, the MACD histogram is negative and still expanding at −1.538, and RSI at 49.74 shows no positive divergence — i.e., no downside exhaustion, continuation until proven otherwise. The plan's own asymmetry fails: ~3.0% to the 266.40 first target against ~7.3% to the 239.82 gap edge from 258.63, roughly 0.66:1 against the 247.8 stop. The ATR of 7.482 (still 8.6% above the pre-gap level after a 25% contraction) means a level 0.86 ATR away is noise, which is why a single close above 269.19 must not be treated as confirmation. The event evidence agrees: a named bullish initiation with a $335 target failed to lift the stock the same day — a bullish catalyst absorbed, not rewarded.

Why the fundamental file caps how much weight AMZN deserves. The decisive correction, which the aggressive seat conceded in substance, is that the $650B contractual-obligation stack is a purchase/usage commitment AMZN owes, with $78.1B due inside twelve months against $161.4B TTM OCF — roughly 48% of operating cash flow pre-committed before capex, interest and tax. That removes the "discretionary capex" defense of the $173B program. Supporting it: TTM FCF flipped from +$13.5B to −$11.6B; Q2 capex $54.2B (27% of revenue); LT debt $68.8B → $133.0B in six months (+93%) with ~$81.9B of LTM issuance; interest expense +100% H1 / +155% Q2; cash taxes −44%, flattering OCF optics; and the $122.3B "equity securities without readily determinable fair value" book up 655% in six months with a $50.5B Q2 / $62.8B H1 upward revaluation — ~62–64% of Q2 GAAP EPS — alongside an AOCI move of +$38.1B only $1.6B of which is FX. Core EPS annualizes near $8.00, so at 258.63 AMZN is ~32x core trailing earnings with negative FCF and no buyback or dividend. That is a full growth multiple for a cash-consuming, debt-issuing, mark-to-model balance sheet.

Why Underweight and not Sell, and why not Hold. Undisputed positives forbid liquidation: revenue +19.6% accelerating from +16.6%, operating income +43.2% to $27.5B, margin 13.7%, OCF +33.2% to $161.4B, D&A of $75.2B (+32%) already running and margin still expanding — prior capex vintages are earning — plus $176.1B of cash/AFS, net cash ex-leases, and price 3.57% above a rising 50-SMA (249.73) and 8.52% above a rising 200-SMA (238.33) with the golden cross intact. That structure is exactly why this is a trim rather than an exit or a short. Hold at full weight is the worst-priced option: 100 units through a 257.04–266.40 flag whose first target is 3% away and whose downside is 7%+ is a directional long with no stop.

On sizing I side with the conservative and neutral seats against the aggressive one. The aggressive's "stop selling and re-add above 269.19" plan would sell 262.75 and buy back 2.5% higher with no fundamental risk reduced — a 0.66:1 payoff critique that applies identically to his own re-entry. But the conservative's demand for two consecutive closes plus a weekly close before re-entry risks converting a disciplined trim into a permanent underweight inside an intact intermediate uptrend, and his blanket 50%-of-target ceiling with no portfolio context is arbitrary. With portfolio context explicitly unknown, I size to the lower half of the range but keep a real core: trim 40–50% to 50–60 units, front-load half near market, hold the rest behind the 256.93/249.73 triggers, and allow one bounded re-entry tranche (one-quarter to one-third) on the neutral's confirmation set.

What would change the call. Upward toward Hold/Overweight: a close above 269.19 on >50M shares with a positive MACD histogram and the next session holding 266.40 (then re-add one-quarter to one-third); a higher low at 249.73–251.0 on expanding volume with a reclaim of 256.93 and 262.75; or fundamental proof — capex-to-revenue flat or falling, TTM FCF turning positive, debt issuance decelerating, D&A decelerating as a share of revenue, or any transaction validating the $122.3B private marks. Downward toward minimal/zero regardless of moving averages: next 10-Q showing capex-to-revenue still rising, total debt above ~$150B, or any material markdown in the equity-stake book; also a decisive break below 249.73 on expanding volume — do not catch the 239.82–238.33 gap-fill/200-SMA zone until it stabilizes and reclaims 262.75 with a higher low.

Stated data gaps: no AWS segment revenue, margin or backlog, so the AWS-re-acceleration justification for capex and the "commitment stack is a demand signal" rebuttal are both unverified; no live valuation multiples, so the ~32x core figure is derived from management's stated core EPS and must be re-checked against a live quote before sizing; news coverage is materially incomplete (only 08-20 records supplied, 112 of 132 eligible records unsupplied), so the Rosenblatt catalyst is de-weighted and the observed poor reaction, not the headline, is what I used; and no portfolio, holdings or cash context was supplied, so all sizing is expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should flex with AI-capex concentration elsewhere in the book.

**Price Target**: 250.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the next 10-Q

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of +2.5% (raw +3.0%) says the Underweight directional call was wrong in this window, though five days is too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis. This undercuts the “near-term tape is broken, front-load the trim near market” leg, since selling at 258–262 missed the bounce, while it supports keeping a core and not shorting given the rising 50/200-SMAs. The lesson for next time is to separate tactical trim timing from the strategic Underweight: with price only 0.86 ATR from invalidation and MACD negative, use a smaller first tranche and require failure at 262.75/266.40 or a close below 256.93 before adding to the trim.
